international.title: DOJ warns Elizabeth Warren over Trump investigations – US politics live
international.summary: Letter to likely chair of Senate Banking Committee is latest warning to Democrats about their potential plans following midterms success Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer , asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances. Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade. Donald Trump is preparing to depart for Asia on Monday, turning his focus to economic deals and historic three-way nuclear talks with Russia and China as his administration adjusts to a new political reality in Washington. Trump’s departure comes after the often-omnipresent president had remained largely out of public sight for the past several days. Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances. Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade. US air travel disruptions continued for a third day with more than 10,000 flights affected on Sunday, but transportation secretary Sean Duffy predicted a return to normal by Monday even as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule following a systemwide ground stop. After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024. Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.
